text: 🇲🇽🚆 "Today's inauguration carries one word. Beyond the great work, because it is a work of Mexican engineering, after many years of abandonment of Mexican engineering too... it is a word that the Fourth Transformation of public life brought with it: justice. And alongside that word goes the word well-being." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, La Concordia, Chiapas On November 7 she opened the Rizo de Oro bridge over the La Angostura reservoir. Infrastructure Secretary Jesús Antonio Esteva: 408 m long, 2 km with its road accesses, the first mixed steel-and-concrete arch bridge in Mexico, built by Mexican companies. 27 steel segments of about 100 tons each were mounted by cableway from 93 m temporary towers. It generated 5,700 jobs. Load-tested with the UNAM Engineering Institute and the Mexican Transport Institute, it will be instrumented to monitor deformations in real time. Begun under López Obrador, finished under Sheinbaum.

🇲🇽🎨 "Education is a right. Education is not a commodity. Education is not a privilege that only those with economic resources can pay for." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ocozocoautla, Chiapas In Ocozocoautla on November 6, she recalled the 1986–87 UNAM student movement: the rector's reform raised tuition and fees, and a propaganda campaign called students lazy. Students demanded a public debate, broadcast on Radio Universidad, chanted that slogan by the tens of thousands, filled the Zócalo and struck until the authorities repealed every reform. "40 years later, and I never imagined I would be president of the Republic, we defend the same thing." She traced the right to public education to José María Morelos, Benito Juárez and the Mexican Revolution, "and who else defends public education? You, the young people of Mexico."

🇲🇽🎨 "You open TikTok and start swiping at the screen. And suddenly an hour has passed. And suddenly two hours. It is a form of addiction. It is like a drug." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas At the National Day for Peace on November 6, she said her government studied why depression and anxiety have risen among young people who lived the COVID lockdown in primary school and then the boom of social media and artificial intelligence. They spoke with engineers, many of them Mexican, who left very high-paying positions at Meta and TikTok "because they realized that the creation of the algorithms asks those who create them to generate addiction." Even much of the content is now made with AI: "It is not even created by a person anymore." Her response: talk about it in schools with the ABC of Emotions.

🇲🇽✊ "They criticize us because we say that all students deserve a scholarship. All of them." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ocozocoautla, Chiapas As head of government of Mexico City she found a "talented children" scholarship only for students with 9 and 10 averages. A study showed it did not push the others to get better grades. Instead it split the classroom between the "supposed good student" and the "supposed bad student." After giving scholarships to every primary and secondary student, all of them got better grades, learned more and dropped out less. Chiapas now covers every student from primary through university: 1,219,971 students, an investment of over 9.2 billion pesos. She also announced a medical and nursing school for the Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos campus in Comitán.

text: 🇲🇽✊ "Father Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla said no to castes, no to slavery. Benito Juárez García said we are all equal before the law. Nobody is more than anyone else." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas Closing the National Day for Peace at CONALEP 22 in Chiapa de Corzo, she said the goal of talking about emotions in school is to keep young people away from drugs and alcohol, "which is also a drug," to build peace and friendship, and above all to recognize "that we are all great people, that nobody is less than anyone else." During the colony, she noted, there were castes, "those who were worth more and those who were worth less." "Each one of us is a different person, but we have the right to the same."
